To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
biodegradable coffee jar lids made of PLA and banana fiber composites have lower global warming potential and fossil energy consumption compared to the conventional polyethylene (PE) lids.
biocomposite lids made from banana fiber and PLA have lower global warming and acidification potential, and higher abiotic depletion potential, than lids made from conventional plastics.
biocomposite lids have a lower environmental impact than their plastic counterparts, and the use of banana fiber in biocomposite lids can reduce the environmental impact even further.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of biocomposite lids for coffee jars.
the comparative life cycle assessment (LCA) of coffee jar lids produced from biocomposites based on poly (lactic) acid (PLA) and banana fiber (BF).
comparative life cycle assessment of two different biocomposites containing PLA (poly(lactic acid)) and banana fiber, used for the production of coffee jar lids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
banana fiber based biodegradable composite lids are a more environmentally benign alternative to the conventional lids.
the use of banana fiber in the manufacture of coffee jar lids has a significant environmental benefit compared to the use of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) lids.
the banana fiber composite lids are a better alternative than conventional plastic lids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the banana fiber based composite lids have a lower impact on global warming, ozone depletion, photochemical ozone creation, acidification, eutrophication, and fossil fuel use compared to the polypropylene lids.
biocomposite lids made of poly(lactic acid) and natural fiber have the potential to reduce environmental impacts in the life cycle of packaging.
banana fiber biocomposite lids are more environmentally benign than their petroleum based counterpart.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the life cycle of biocomposite lids is dominated by the energy consumption in the manufacturing stage, while the use stage is the most important for the global warming potential.
banana fiber based biodegradable packaging materials can be a good substitute for traditional petroleum-based plastics.
the use of natural fibers in packaging applications is a viable alternative to conventional plastics.
